Established in 1937 by the German Labour Front, it was revived after World War II by British Army officer Ivan Hirst and, over the 81 years since, grew into the global brand it is today. The company is well known for the Beetle and serves as the flagship brand of its eponymous conglomerate "Conglomerate (company)"), the Volkswagen Group, which was the world's largest automotive manufacturer by global sales in 2016 and 2017. Ferdinand Porsche, a well-known designer for high-end vehicles and race cars, had been trying for years to get a manufacturer interested in a small car suitable for a family. He built a car known as the *Volksauto* from the ground up in 1933, using many popular ideas and several of his own, putting together a car with an air-cooled rear engine, torsion bar suspension, and a "beetle" shape, the front bonnet rounded for better aerodynamics (necessary as it had a small engine).

title: Volkswagen AG | Business and Management | Research Starters
content: The company has shifted its focus toward electric vehicles, with plans to introduce multiple new electric models by 2026, aiming for 70% of its sales in Europe to be electric. Volkswagen AG, commonly known as Volkswagen or VW, is a prominent German automotive manufacturer headquartered in Wolfsburg, Lower Saxony. Founded on May 28, 1937, by the German Labour Front, the company was initially established to produce an affordable "people's car" as envisioned by Adolf Hitler. Over the decades, Volkswagen expanded its portfolio by acquiring various luxury brands, including Audi, Porsche, Bentley, and Lamborghini, which helped solidify its position as one of the largest automakers globally. Known as Volkswagenwerk, or "The People's Car Company" at the time, to provide the design for this "people's car," the German Labor Front called in the Austrian automotive engineer Ferdinand Porsche. Founded in 1937 by the German government to mass-produce a low-priced “people’s car,” Volkswagen Group, aka Volkswagen AG, whose headquarters are in Wolfsburg, Germany, is a leading German carmaker. The company was the world’s largest car manufacturer in 2016 and 2017, based on the number of global sales and in 2019, the Volkswagen Group grew its worldwide deliveries by 1.3 percent to 10,974,600 vehicles. Over the years, Volkswagen became a symbol of Germany’s economic miracle and went on to operate plants all over the world, including in Mexico, Brazil, China, and the United States.
